latin: Cum paucōs diēs Rōmae commorēmur et parum temporis igitur habeāmus, mōnstrātōre ūtāmur, quī nōbīs rēs praecipuās ostendat et illūstret.
— Ecce! Peropportūne adest* mōnstrātor. Hic nōbīs ūtilissimus erit.
Dīc, quaesō, optimē vir, quae possumus* hodiē celeriter invīsere?
— Prīmum ad templum Sānctō Petrō dicātum vōs dūcam, quod, ut omnibus est nōtum, maximum est Chrīstiānitātis.
— Eugē! Cupiditāte flagrāmus id videndī. Nūlla mora facta, raedā meritōriā petāmus celeberrimum templum!
— Quae est templī magnificentia et mōlēs!
— Amplissima platēa, quam ante oculōs habēmus, utrāque parte porticū<sup>1</sup> circumdata est in apside<sup>2</sup> curvāta, et columnīs suspēnsa.
Aedificium sustinet magnum illum tholum<sup>3</sup>, quī altē ēminet et ab omnibus urbis regiōnibus aspicitur.
Tholus metra centum trīgintā duo patet in altitūdinem, duo et quadrāgintā in lātitūdinem.
Spatium medium templī tantā est amplitūdine ut, cum in eō consistis, vagus<sup>4</sup> et sōlus videāris et timor quīdam religiōsus tē perfundat<sup>5</sup>.
Ālae dextrā et sinistrā multās habent aediculās<sup>6</sup> tabulīs pictīs et marmore ōrnātās.
Mīrō splendōre est lacunar, aurō distīnctum<sup>7</sup> et colōribus splendidīs ōrnātum.
Praetereā statuae marmoreae, mīrābilī artificiō perfectae, sunt omnibus in partibus collocātae, quae Sānctōrum et Pontificum imāginēs reddunt.
Animadvertite praeclārum altāre<sup>8</sup>, quod in mediā basilicā sē attollit<sup>9</sup>: in eō nūllī sacerdōtī, praeter Pontificem<sup>10</sup>, missam celebrāre licet.
Tempus, malum!, fūgit et iam<sup>11</sup> hōra statūta adest*, quā templī valvae clauduntur nec iam licet in summum tholum ascendere, unde longē lātēque patet prōspectus pulcherrimus.
latinAccented: Cum paucōs diēs Rōmae commorḗmur et parum témporis ígitur habeā́mus, mōnstrātṓre ūtā́mur, quī nōbīs rēs praecípuās osténdat et illū́stret.
— Ecce! Peropportū́ne adest* mōnstrā́tor. Hic nōbīs ūtilíssimus erit.
Dīc, quaesō, óptimē vir, quae póssumus* hódiē celériter invī́sere?
— Prīmum ad templum Sānctō Petrō dicā́tum vōs dūcam, quod, ut ómnibus est nōtum, máximum est Chrīstiānitā́tis.
— Éugē! Cupiditā́te flagrā́mus id vidéndī. Nūlla mora facta, raedā meritṓriā petā́mus celebérrimum templum!
— Quae est templī magnificéntia et mōlēs!
— Amplíssima platḗa, quam ante óculōs habḗmus, utrā́que parte pórticū<sup>1</sup> circúmdata est in ápside<sup>2</sup> curvā́ta, et colúmnīs suspḗnsa.
Aedifícium sústinet magnum illum tholum<sup>3</sup>, quī altē ḗminet et ab ómnibus urbis regiṓnibus aspícitur.
Tholus metra centum trīgíntā duo patet in altitū́dinem, duo et quadrāgíntā in lātitū́dinem.
Spátium médium templī tantā est amplitū́dine ut, cum in eō consístis, vagus<sup>4</sup> et sōlus videā́ris et timor quīdam religiṓsus tē perfúndat<sup>5</sup>.
Ālae dextrā et sinístrā multās habent aedículās<sup>6</sup> tábulīs pictīs et mármore ōrnā́tās.
Mīrō splendṓre est lácunar, aurō distī́nctum<sup>7</sup> et colṓribus spléndidīs ōrnā́tum.
Praetéreā státuae marmóreae, mīrā́bilī artifíciō perféctae, sunt ómnibus in pártibus collocā́tae, quae Sānctṓrum et Pontíficum imā́ginēs reddunt.
Animadvértite praeclā́rum altā́re<sup>8</sup>, quod in médiā basílicā sē attóllit<sup>9</sup>: in eō nūllī sacerdṓtī, praeter Pontíficem<sup>10</sup>, missam celebrā́re licet.
Tempus, malum!, fūgit et iam<sup>11</sup> hōra statū́ta adest*, quā templī valvae claudúntur nec iam licet in summum tholum ascéndere, unde longē lātḗque patet prōspéctus pulchérrimus.
english: As we [are only staying] in Rome a few days, and so we have little time, let us [have recourse] to a guide, who [will show] us the most important things and [give us explanations] (show and enlighten, subj. pres.).
— There! A guide [presents himself] very opportunely. This one will be very useful to us.
Tell [us], I beg you (excellent man), what can we see today quickly?
— First, I will take you to [the Basilica of] (temple) Saint Peter (dedicated), which as [is known] (by) everybody, is the biggest of Christendom.
— Very good! We are burning with desire to see it. Without any delay (made) let us go (subj. pres.) by taxi to the famous basilica!
— What [splendour] (is of the temple) and [what imposing] mass!
— The immense square which we have before our eyes is surrounded on both sides by a [semicircular] gallery (curved in apse) and is supported by columns.
The building supports this great dome which rises high and which can be seen from all the quarters of the city.
The dome [rises] 132 m in height [and] extends 42 m in width.
The interior (middle space) of the church is of such size that, when (you) [find yourself] in it, [you feel] lost and alone (you are seen, subj. pres.), and a religious fear [invades] (you invades).
The right and left wings include numerous chapels, decorated with pictures (painted) and [statues of] marble.
The ceiling is of remarkable beauty, plated with gold and decorated with brilliant colours.
Moreover, marble statues, made with admirable technique, are placed on all sides, which represent the [images of the] saints and of the popes.
Notice this magnificent altar, which rises in the middle of the basilica: there, no priest is allowed, except the Pope, to celebrate mass.

Time, alas, passes, and there is already the prescribed hour at which the doors are closed (of the temple) and it is no longer permitted to climb to the top of the dome from where a very beautiful view opens in all directions (far and wide).

footnotes: Porticus, -us, f., gallery with columns, portico.
Apsis, -idis, f.: semicircular enclosure adjoining a room or a building (apse); orbit of a planet (in cosmography, the apsides are particular points of the orbit).
Tholus, -i, m., dome, vault of a temple; the vault, in general, is said fornix, -icis, m.
Vagus, -a, -um, wandering, lost; vagari, to wander.
Perfundo, -is, -ere, fudi, fusum, to pour into or over, to soak, to penetrate.
Aedicula, -ae, f., small temple, chapel; diminutive of aedes which, in the SINGULAR, means the temple.
Distinguo, -is, -ere, tinxi, tinctum, to separate, to distinguish, to adorn.
Altar, or altare, -is, n., altar; one also says ara, -ae, f.
Attollo, -is, -ere (neither pft, nor supine), to lift towards (ad tollere); tollo, -is, -ere, sustuli, sublatum, to lift, to raise, to make disappear.
Pontifex, -icis, m., priest, pontiff, and in Christendom, the Pope (cf. L. 94, P. 13).
Iam = jam; we have here respected the usual spelling in Italy, where one uses the v but not the j; you see that this change presents no difficulty.
comments: Today and tomorrow, the lesson is intended to give you some additional information on the visit of Rome, sketched in the previous lesson, and, on the same occasion, on the spelling used in Italy.

Misenum, -i, n. (promuntorium), (Cape) Misenum: Cf. L. 97, P. 7. — Neapolis, -is, f., Naples. — Septentrio, -onis, m. (minor): one of the two constellations of seven stars (= septem triones, the seven plough oxen) and which is called, in cosmography, Ursa Minor, the Little Bear, whence the North; the other being Septentrio (Ursa) major, the Great Bear. Oriens and Occidens are drawn from the present participles of the verbs oriri, to rise, and occidere, to fall, to die (ob + cadere, supine occasum), which must not be confused with occidere (i long, supine occisum), to strike, to kill, which comes from caedere, to cut. Auster, -tri, m., south wind, and, by extension, the south. — Amplector, -eris, -i, plexus sum, to surround, to embrace, that is to say to hold in one's arms. To embrace with the mouth is said osculari (osculum, small mouth or kiss). — Jugum, -i, n., the yoke (from jungere, to join). Here, idea of junction between two mountains, two valleys or two slopes. — Culmen, -inis, n., the summit, culminating point. One also says cacumen, same declension. — Tellus, -uris, f., the Earth (more or less deified), the soil (cf. the adj. fr. tellurique). — The metals of P. 14 are all neuters in um, -i. The corresponding adjectives are all in eus, ea, eum (ferreus, of iron, etc.). Carbo, -onis, m., coal; adamas, adamantis, m., diamond. — Rivus, -i, m., river; rivulus, stream; amnis, -is, m., big watercourse, river. Flumen and fluvius are less precise terms (idea of current, of fluere). — Metallum, -i, n., the mine or the metal; metalla, -orum, n., the mine(s); damnare in metallum or condemnare ad metalla, to condemn to forced labour in a mine.

latin: Quid est Mīsēnum?
Est prōmuntorium prope Neāpolim situm.
Quā in caelī regiōne? — Ad Occidentem spectāns.
Quae sunt cēterae caelī regiōnēs? — Sunt Septentriō, Oriēns, et Merīdiēs seu Auster.
Austrālia est īnsula in hēmisphaeriō austrālī sita, ubi Canga, marsupiālis lēctiōnis 79ae, nāta est.
Hispānia est paenīnsula quae Hibēria dīcitur.
Sinus Ligusticus est illa pars maris quam lītus ligusticum amplectitur, vel Liguriae ōra maritima, quae in arcum curvāta est.
Hujus lītoris portūs praecipuus Genua est.
Cum via inter montēs duōs trānsit, quōmodo pars ejus summa vocātur? — Jugum vocātur, sed hoc nōmen apud nōnnūllōs auctōrēs montem ipsum summum dēsignat.
Ante et post jugum, via vallem saepe sequitur.
Montium culmina nive candent.
Saxa abrupta faucibus ēminent.
Sēmitā ponte ligneō rīvum trānsit et ad metalla dūcit.
Tellūs hōrum montium ferrō, cuprō, stannō, plumbō, aurō, carbōne, adamante, abundat. In hīs montibus, ferrum, cuprum, stannum, plumbum, aurum abundanter nāscuntur.
Hae dīvitiae simul in ūnō locō invenīrī nōn possunt.
Eugē! Nātūrālem historiam bene nōvistī.
latinAccented: Quid est Mīsḗnum?
Est prōmuntórium prope Neā́polim situm.
Quā in caelī regiṓne? — Ad Occidéntem spectāns.
Quae sunt cḗterae caelī regiṓnēs? — Sunt Septéntriō, Óriēns, et Merī́diēs seu Auster.
Austrā́lia est ī́nsula in hēmispháeriō austrā́lī sita, ubi Canga, marsupiā́lis lēctiṓnis 79ae, nāta est.
Hispā́nia est paenī́nsula quae Hibḗria dī́citur.
Sinus Ligústicus est illa pars maris quam lītus ligústicum ampléctitur, vel Ligúriae ōra marítima, quae in arcum curvā́ta est.
Hujus lī́toris portūs praecípuus Génua est.
Cum via inter montēs duōs trānsit, quṓmodo pars ejus summa vocā́tur? — Jugum vocā́tur, sed hoc nōmen apud nōnnū́llōs auctṓrēs montem ipsum summum dēsígnat.
Ante et post jugum, via vallem saepe séquitur.
Móntium cúlmina nive candent.
Saxa abrúpta fáucibus ḗminent.
Sḗmitā ponte lígneō rīvum trānsit et ad metálla dūcit.
Tellūs hōrum móntium ferrō, cuprō, stannō, plumbō, aurō, carbṓne, adamánte, abúndat. In hīs móntibus, ferrum, cuprum, stannum, plumbum, aurum abundánter nāscúntur.
Hae dīvítiae simul in ūnō locō invenī́rī nōn possunt.
Éugē! Nātūrā́lem históriam bene nōvístī.
english: What is Misenum?
It is a cape situated near Naples.
In what [direction] (regions of the sky)? — To the west (looking).
What are the other cardinal points? — They are the north, the east and the south.
Australia is an island situated in the southern hemisphere, where Kanga, the kangaroo of lesson 79, was born.
Spain is a peninsula which is also called Iberia.
The gulf [of Genoa] (Ligurian) is that part of the sea which the Ligurian coast embraces, or the maritime border of Liguria, which is curved [in the shape of] an arc.
The most important port of this coast is Genoa.
When a road passes between two mountains, what is its highest part called? — A pass (is called), but this name designates in some authors the upper part of the mountain itself.
Before and after the pass, the road often follows a valley.
The summits of the mountains are white with snow.
Abrupt rocks dominate the defile.
The path crosses the river by a wooden bridge and leads to the mine(s).

The soil of these mountains abounds in iron, copper, tin, lead, gold, coal and diamond. In these mountains, iron, copper, tin, lead, gold, etc., are found [in abundant deposits] (abundantly are born).
These riches cannot be found at once in a single place.
Bravo! You know natural history well.
